rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The theme with your name on it Career is the unit students read most closely, for obvious reasons — the reader is choosing, or about to choose. The honest frame is that a career is neither a lottery nor a ladder but a **portfolio**: education, skills, connections, reputation and luck, built over years.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
CV and job-application language is tested — revise formal register and format.
Match personal skills to job requirements explicitly in answers.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## The debates, held honestly **"Follow your passion" versus "follow the market".** The romance says passion sustains effort; the pragmatist says passion does not pay in a saturated field. The synthesis worth writing: passion determines *what* you will be good at, the market determines *whether* it pays — and the durable careers find the overlap, or build it (a hobby that becomes a trade, a skill that creates its…  ·  ## Grammar and style: the tense of your own story The **present perfect** is the working life's home tense — "I **have completed** my +2", "I **have worked** as a tutor **for** two years" — because it ties the past to the present application. The **simple past** dates the finished chapter ("I **joined** the club in 2079").…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## How the exam asks it The **application letter** (6–8 marks) is near-guaranteed: an advertisement is given, you apply. Checklist the format first (addresses, date, salutation, subject line, close), then purpose in line one, then two proofs shaped to the role. The **CV-writing task** wants reverse-chronological order, action verbs (*led, organised, trained*), no full sentences, no photo-of-your-personality prose.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Write a cover letter for a teaching vacancy. (4 marks) — format, post and source, two matching qualifications, availability.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Q. How should you answer 'tell me about yourself' in an interview? (2 marks) — brief education, relevant skills, one achievement — under a minute.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The words that carry the theme The vocabulary of work sorts into layers. **The search:** vacancy, opening, candidate, applicant, CV (curriculum vitae — the story of your working life in two pages), cover letter, interview, shortlist, appointment. **The working life:** profession, occupation, career path, promotion, increment, resignation, retirement, internship, apprenticeship, freelance, shift.…  ·  ## Reading the theme like a writer — the language of applications An application letter is **persuasion with a format**, and the format is the easy half: your address and the date, the employer's address, a salutation (*Dear Sir or Madam* when the name is unknown, *Dear Ms Sharma* when it is not), the purpose in the first line, the evidence in the middle, the polite close (*Yours faithfully* with the unknown name,…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Career questions test FORMAL WRITING: cover letter and CV conventions — follow the fixed format; content must match the advertised post.  ·  Trick 2: Interview answers use the STAR frame: Situation, Task, Action, Result — one compact STAR example beats vague claims.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. How should you answer 'tell me about yourself' in an interview? (2 marks) — brief education, relevant skills, one achievement — under a minute.
